Debug (via Postman): json CopyEdit { "error": "invalid_grant", "error_description": "Invalid credentials / User does not have access to any facility" } Root Cause: The Uniware API user was not assigned any facility . Fix: Log into Uniware Admin → Users → Edit the API User → Assign at least one Facility (e.g., WH001). Without this, authentication cannot succeed. 2. Sales Order Sync Setup Steps: In Unicommerce Settings : Enable Sales Order Sync Set sync frequency (30–60 minutes recommended) Set default: Naming series Customer group Create Unicommerce Channel(s) for each marketplace.Navigate to: Unicommerce Channel → New Provide: Channel Name (must match exactly as in Uniware) Default Company, Warehouse, Accounts, etc. Set Enabled = True Issue #2: Orders Not Syncing Despite Setup Symptom: No orders created in ERPNext. title: Issue with Financial Statements for 366 days Fiscal Year (Nepal)
first_post: In Nepal, the fiscal year runs from 2024-07-16 to 2025-07-16 , which makes it a 13-month period (longer than 365 days). This seems to be causing errors or inconsistencies in the Financial Statements generated by ERPNext. I have already enabled the “Is Short/Long Year” option in the Fiscal Year settings, but the reports still don’t reflect the data correctly. Has anyone else faced this issue or found a workaround for handling non-standard fiscal years in ERPNext?
full_text: In Nepal, the fiscal year runs from 2024-07-16 to 2025-07-16 , which makes it a 13-month period (longer than 365 days). This seems to be causing errors or inconsistencies in the Financial Statements generated by ERPNext. I have already enabled the “Is Short/Long Year” option in the Fiscal Year settings, but the reports still don’t reflect the data correctly. Has anyone else faced this issue or found a workaround for handling non-standard fiscal years in ERPNext? Hi July 16 to July 16 can’t be a valid fiscal year because the start and end can’t share the same date. Even if you intend to end at "midnight of July 16, most accounting systems and legal frameworks do not accept same day as closing for predecessor year and on the other hand opening for the next. ERPNext does not support this things as well. IFRS Standard References IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements : Requires disclosing the period covered but doesn’t dictate dates. IAS 10 Events After the Reporting Period : Considers the period-end as a fixed date (e.g., Dec 31, not Jan 1). The problem is that they’re only the same dates in the Gregorian calendar. In the Nepali calendar, 16 July 2024 and 16 July 2025 are in different months. Thank you @ahsantareen and @peterg for your helpful insights. To clarify, Nepal follows the Vikram Samvat (VS) calendar, not the Gregorian one. The fiscal year runs from 1st Shrawan to end of Asadh , typically translating to 16 July to 16 July or 17 July to 16 July Though it appears as the same date in the Gregorian calendar for 16 to 16 case, in the Nepali system these are distinct and fall in different months and years. If anyone here has dealt with similar challenges of managing Nepal’s 13-month fiscal years or non-standard fiscal periods in ERPNext, I’d really appreciate hearing how you addressed them. What workarounds or customizations did you find effective? Your insights or examples would be a great help to the community—thank you! Solved this with no issues, just tick on short than 12 month check box, you are good to go

Not Frappe/ERPNext based, but might integrate and fit well. Short answer: yes—Mautic and Frappe/ERPNext integrate well, but there’s no up-to-date “official” plug-and-play app. You’ll typically do it via APIs + webhooks or an orchestration layer like n8n. What “native” options exist? A historical app from Dokos mapped Mautic ⇄ ERPNext objects (Contacts, Companies, Segments) and OAuth2 auth. It’s archived and targeted Frappe/ERPNext v10–11, so expect breakage on modern stacks (v14–v16). Good for design references, not drop-in use. Community threads confirm the old app no longer works on recent versions and that people now integrate via webhooks/APIs or iPaaS (n8n). Two viable integration patterns A) Direct (no n8n) — Webhooks + REST on both sides From Mautic → ERPNext: Use Mautic Webhooks (contact created/updated, email events, page hits, form submits) to POST into ERPNext endpoints (custom whitelisted server method or API) to create/update Lead/Contact/Communication and log activities. From ERPNext → Mautic: Use ERPNext Webhooks on DocTypes (Lead/Contact/Customer/Opportunity) or call Mautic’s REST to upsert contacts, add to segments, push events/notes. Docs you’ll rely on Mautic Webhooks (events + payload shape). Frappe/ERPNext REST & webhook guides for creating/updating docs via API safely (not direct DB). When to pick this: small scope, you control both servers, you’ll code the mapping and retries. B) With n8n (recommended for most teams) n8n ships first-class nodes for Mautic and ERPNext; build bi-directional flows, handle auth, mapping, branching, deduping, retries, and audit logs in a visual way. Typical pattern: Webhook (trigger) → Transform/Match → ERPNext (create/update) and vice-versa. Unified Lead Lifecycle (website → nurture → CRM) Mautic forms/campaigns capture and score; qualified leads are auto-created in ERPNext (Lead/Contact + Segment/UTM fields), with an assigned Sales rep and ToDo reminders. Behavior-driven Sales tasks On campaign events (e.g., download, email click, score threshold), call ERPNext to create ToDo/Opportunity and attach the trace as Communication/Timeline. Account enrichment & clean lists Sync ERPNext Customers/Contacts → Mautic to keep segments current for re-engagement, cross-sell, and win-back—mirror of the archived app’s mapping. Closed-loop attribution Push Opportunity/Quotation/Invoice status from ERPNext back to Mautic to close the loop on campaigns and calculate lead-to-revenue. (ERPNext webhook/API out; Mautic REST in.) Transactional + marketing separation Keep ERPNext for transactional comms; run marketing journeys in Mautic (multichannel, scoring, web tracking) while synchronizing consent and contact state. Implementation notes & gotchas Model mappings: Start with Leads/Contacts/Companies/Segments; mirror the Dokos mapping for a head start, then extend. Auth: Prefer OAuth2 or API keys; in ERPNext expose whitelisted methods rather than touching DB directly. Idempotency & dedupe: Use stable external IDs (e.g., mautic_contact_id in ERPNext and erpnext_name in Mautic). Retries/queueing: Mautic can queue webhooks; n8n provides retries and error handling—major reliability win. PDPL/GDPR: Centralize consent; sync opt-in/out flags both ways. Version reality: Don’t depend on the archived plugin in production; treat it as reference (OAuth2 flow, field maps). Is there any updates on this with regards to capabilities in the Frappe Ecosystem? As far as I know Frappe CRM is planning to implement Marketing Campaigns. I assume the Campaign functionality in ERPNext is largely being phased out?

Bottom line is it returns the wrong qty, i wrote some utility functions that actually return the correct qty in my custom app, if someone needs it hit me up. x = frappe.call( 'erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001', warehouse='Finished Goods - T', inventory_dimensions_dict={'customer': 'test'} ) print(x) A few important notes: Use the code (not the name) of both the item and the inventory dimension Doctype. This fieldname is based on the Doctype name in lowercase , not the display name you gave to the dimension. For example, if you create an inventory dimension called “Customer Inventory Dimension” , the fieldname will simply be: customer and not : custom_customer_inventory_dimension or customer_inventory_dimension as one might expect. Asset Category controls depreciation and accounting of assets particularly. Since Assets are not tradable items does not require to be accounted under stock ledger. Fixed Asset Register is there to replace stock ledger. You can only move an asset and turn into stock item by working with Asset Capitalization where entry type has to be Decapitalization. You need to use Asset Movement if you’d like to change assignment or location type details of the asset. are you refering to something like this??? github.com/frappe/erpnext Move Asset Between Companies Without Changing Asset Code (Fresh Depreciation in New Company) opened 06:31AM - 25 Apr 25 UTC maveezmh feature-request I'd like to request a feature enhancement that allows transferring an asset from … one company to another without changing the asset code, while resetting depreciation in the new company and maintaining historical traceability. Depreciation history is fragmented. Proposed Feature A "Transfer to Another Company" action on the Asset form. The same asset code should be retained in the destination company for traceability. title: Item "Valuation Rate" shows as 0, but exists on Item Price and Stock Entry
first_post: When I view an item, the Valuation shows as 0. image 1057×334 23.8 KB On Stock Entry, we did give this item a value. image 1036×113 10.5 KB This is behavior normal or is it a bug? If it’s normal and intended, how do you add Valuation Rate so that it would show after stock entry?
full_text: When I view an item, the Valuation shows as 0. image 1057×334 23.8 KB On Stock Entry, we did give this item a value. image 1036×113 10.5 KB This is behavior normal or is it a bug? If it’s normal and intended, how do you add Valuation Rate so that it would show after stock entry? Anyone have any idea? This field is misleading. It does not represent the current valuation rate of the item based on stock transactions. Instead, it is a default valuation rate that is used during stock transactions, only if no other valuation data exists (e.g., if the item has no prior stock or transactions, no item prices, …). This field’s value is manually set and does not update automatically.

title: Please help recommend the hardware configuration for building the server
first_post: Hello everyone, I am a beginner to ERPNext. I would like to ask you to help me recommend the hardware configuration of a server. I am a pharmaceutical machinery manufacturing factory, and I only need to use the functions of purchasing, sales, production, and HR. There are about 200 employees, and there are 50,000 different types of parts in the warehouse to manage. I’m thinking about building a stable, high-speed server myself. Do you have friends who can give good advice? Thank you!
full_text: Hello everyone, I am a beginner to ERPNext. I would like to ask you to help me recommend the hardware configuration of a server. I am a pharmaceutical machinery manufacturing factory, and I only need to use the functions of purchasing, sales, production, and HR. There are about 200 employees, and there are 50,000 different types of parts in the warehouse to manage. I’m thinking about building a stable, high-speed server myself. Do you have friends who can give good advice? Thank you! If you are going for bare-metal setup, buy the best thing you can afford. Capacity, redundancy, storage, backups, networking, fire safety, power backups, etc. It is time-consuming and takes lot of downtime to upgrade bare-metal servers. If you are going with cloud providers, start with 2CPU, 4GB RAM VM and upgrade as needed, it will upgrade with click of a button with least downtime and no screwdriver needed. Frappecloud being one of the cloud provider you can start with their base plans and then upgrade as you need. Thank you very much! Even if you are building a server, you should strongly consider virtualization. Virtual Machines are easier to backup and restore. Virtualization also allows you to have multiple servers running on a single host. This allows you to have testing, deployment, and production servers. I agree with @volkswagner as well. We have a proxmox setup and everything is fluid! Do not forget also Docker on bare-metal or Cloud. K Thank you very much!

title: Issue with India Compliance App – GSTIN Not Recognized
first_post: After installing the India Compliance app and entering the GSTIN/UIN in the company details, the status is showing as “Not Available.” Additionally, when attempting to create an invoice using the GST item tax template provided by the app, an error appears stating: “Company GSTIN is a mandatory field for GST Transactions.” Could you please assist in resolving this issue?
full_text: After installing the India Compliance app and entering the GSTIN/UIN in the company details, the status is showing as “Not Available.” Additionally, when attempting to create an invoice using the GST item tax template provided by the app, an error appears stating: “Company GSTIN is a mandatory field for GST Transactions.” Could you please assist in resolving this issue? Is GSTIN set in the company address? If not it may raise the said error. GST Status refresh consumes API, and may have been disabled in your GST settings, hence you are seeing status as Not Available. Thank you for your prompt response. After setting the GSTIN in the company address, the error has been resolved.

title: Best Practices for Tracking Field Changes and Updating Submitted Docs in Frappe
first_post: Hi everyone, I’m currently working with the Material Request doctype and have encountered a situation I’d like to ask about. When updating a field using the ORM / Doc API , like this: mr = frappe.get_doc("Material Request", mr_name) mr.status = "Received" mr.save() all event hooks such as validate , before_save , and on_update are triggered as expected. However, if I update a field using the DB API directly , like: frappe.db.set_value("Material Request", mr_name, "status", "Received") then none of the ORM event hooks are triggered — which is understandable, since this method bypasses the document lifecycle. I have two main questions: Is there a way to listen for or intercept changes made via frappe.db.set_value() ? For example, I’d like to trigger a function whenever the status field is changed — even if it’s changed using direct DB access. In some cases, I need to update certain fields on submitted documents ( docstatus = 1 ) . Since calling .save() on a submitted doc raises the error "Submitted Document cannot be saved." , the only option seems to be using frappe.db.set_value() . Is there a way to bypass this limitation and still use the ORM safely**, or any other “safe” alternative to update fields on submitted documents? My goals are: To track or respond to field-level changes regardless of whether they’re made through the ORM or frappe.db.set_value() . To safely update allowed fields on submitted documents (like status or custom fields) without relying solely on raw DB operations. Any guidance or best practices would be much appreciated. Thanks in advance!

Hello @SKDragon18 set_value does not trigger any document event.if you want to trigger any document event you need to use doc.save() One option is there if you don’t want to execute all event but want to execute any single one you can try as below. frappe.get_doc(doctype, docname).validate() frappe.db.set_value(doctype, docname, fieldname, value) Alternative for above: doc = frappe.get_doc(doctype, docname) doc.db_set(fieldname, value) doc.save() If you want to change any field after submission and want to use doc.save(), you need to set allow on submit property for that field. Hope this will help you. first_post: Hi everyone, I’m having a persistent issue with Script Reports on my ERPNext instance (ERPNext 15.45.2, Frappe 15.49.1, HRMS 15.35.3, self-hosted on Ubuntu). Problem: No matter what I do, any Script Report I create (even the simplest possible, with just one column and one row) always displays “Nothing to show” or “Generic Empty State”. Query Reports work fine and show data from the database. What I’ve tried so far: Checked all permissions (Administrator user, all necessary permissions on Report, Item, User, etc.) Made sure the report is not “Disabled” Tried different DocTypes (Item, User, Employee) Used the simplest possible script: def execute(filters=None): columns = [{“label”: “Test”, “fieldname”: “test”, “fieldtype”: “Data”}] data = [{“test”: “It works!”}] return columns, data Tried with and without filters, with and without “Is Standard”, in multiple browsers and with different users Ran bench clear-cache , bench restart , bench --site site1.local migrate Checked the Error Log in ERPNext and in the terminal – no errors related to reports In bench console, frappe.get_all("Item", fields=["item_code", "item_name"]) returns data Query Reports with SQL queries work and display data Created a brand new Script Report, no filters, just one column and one value – still nothing shows Additional info: No customizations on the Report DocType No custom scripts that could affect reports Tried incognito mode and a different computer I have tried both official examples from the documentation, community forum scripts, and even some suggestions from AI assistants. Regardless of the source, even the simplest “hello world” Script Report always returns “Nothing to show”. Question: Has anyone experienced this before? Hi @dkumar Once a stock item has had stock transactions (like Purchase Receipts, Stock Entries, or Sales Invoices), you cannot directly enable serialization (i.e., check the “Has Serial No” checkbox) for that item. This is because serialized items require ERPNext to track each unit individually via serial numbers, and any prior transactions without serial numbers break this consistency. On the other hand if you can; Manually update the item via SQL or system/developer console to check “Has Serial No”. Then manually assign serial numbers via Stock Ledger/Serial No Tool . title: Permissions setting for closing sales order
first_post: Hi, I would like to allow my sales staff to close the sales document, but only allow the manager to unclose a document. Can we set it in roles & permissions or do we need coding? I dont see close or unclose function in the permissions manager list.
full_text: Hi, I would like to allow my sales staff to close the sales document, but only allow the manager to unclose a document. Can we set it in roles & permissions or do we need coding? I dont see close or unclose function in the permissions manager list. Hello, I ran into a similar situation before unfortunately, the standard Role Permissions Manager doesn’t let you control the Close and Unclose actions directly, since they aren’t normal field permissions but system-level actions. A simple way to manage this is by creating a custom workflow for the Sales Order. That way, you can control who’s allowed to do what. Here’s a quick idea: Go to Settings > Workflow, and create a new workflow for Sales Order . Add workflow states like: Submitted (sales team can see and work here) Closed (sales team is allowed to close) Reopened (only managers can reopen) Set up transitions: Sales team can move from Submitted → Closed Only managers can go from Closed → Reopened This approach gives you permission control without writing any backend code. Thank you. The weakness of using this process is that the Status will not be offically “Closed” in the system any by workflow and hence you still can create delivery instructions from the Sales Order.

title: How can I export a child table
first_post: Hi, I have added custom input fields and configuration to the Expense Claim Detail child table and need to export these customizations as part of my app so they can be installed on another site where developer mode is disabled . The parent doctype (Expense Claim) exports without issue, but the child table modifications are not being applied on the target site despite trying all the standard approaches. could you please help me
full_text: Hi, I have added custom input fields and configuration to the Expense Claim Detail child table and need to export these customizations as part of my app so they can be installed on another site where developer mode is disabled . The parent doctype (Expense Claim) exports without issue, but the child table modifications are not being applied on the target site despite trying all the standard approaches. could you please help me If you’ve added custom fields to a Doctype—whether a parent (like Expense Claim ) or a child table (like Expense Claim Detail )—and want to move these changes to another site, here are two valid ways to do it: Option 1: Recommended — Use Fixtures This works reliably even in production environments (i.e. when developer_mode = 0 ). Step 1: Customize Using “Customize Form” Go to Customize Form Select the Doctype ( Expense Claim or Expense Claim Detail ) Add your custom fields Save These changes are stored as Custom Field and Property Setter documents. Step 2: Add to Fixtures in hooks.py In your app’s hooks.py : fixtures = [ { "doctype": "Custom Field", "filters": [ ["dt", "in", ["Expense Claim", "Expense Claim Detail"]] ] }, { "doctype": "Property Setter", "filters": [ ["doc_type", "in", ["Expense Claim", "Expense Claim Detail"]] ] } ] Step 3: Export the Fixtures Run: bench export-fixtures This creates JSON files (like custom_field.json , property_setter.json ) inside your app’s /fixtures folder. Step 4: Apply on Another Site Once you install the app or pull changes into another site, just run: bench migrate The fields will be applied automatically — no need for developer mode on the target site. Option 2: Quick Dev Use — Export from Customize Form You can also use the “Export” button at the top right of the Customize Form page. This: Exports your customizations to a JSON file Lets you choose which DocTypes and fields to include Useful for creating manual backups or sharing with a team But note: These JSON files won’t auto-apply on install unless you manually load them or use developer_mode = 1 Not ideal for deployment to staging/production Understanding the Confusion: Parent vs Child Doctype Expense Claim is a parent Doctype Expense Claim Detail is a child table , but it’s still a separate Doctype You must include both in your fixtures or Export if you customize both Child tables aren’t magically included — if you forget to list the child Doctype, its custom fields won’t move.

title: Brand Wise stock Management
first_post: Hello I am using ERPNEXT I have same item from multiple brands. Need to have 1 item from many brand and store stock brand wise. So everytime I have a Stock entry , Need to select the brand. Is it possible in ERPNEXT ?
full_text: Hello I am using ERPNEXT I have same item from multiple brands. Need to have 1 item from many brand and store stock brand wise. So everytime I have a Stock entry , Need to select the brand. Is it possible in ERPNEXT ? Hi @alokkanodia This is very much possible in ERPNext. If you configure Brand as Inventory Dimension, then one item within item master can handle multiple brands at a time. The stock ledger and Balance report will offer stock statuses based on brand then. Please refer to the documentation as well; https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/inventory_dimension Can You help me a bit deeper. I need brand specific to items or item group Not all items have all brands Hi You should follow through; create your custom brand doctype make it inventory dimension tag it on each stock transaction like purchase receipt or delivery note. then you will have stock reports as per brand even though you have used same item. @ahsantareen Custom Doctype Brand Not Needed. Doctype is Already Available in Default. @Nisarg Existing brand doctype will always fetch value from item master and it is not editable on transactional level despite you overrun it by setting property setter. You have to have your own custom doctype for brand to achieve one item with multiple brand recordings.

title: Can we use phone number as the primary info used to authenticate users instead of email?
first_post: I see many discussions requesting a way to let users log in using their phone number. While most people mean authenticating with just a phone number and OTP, the solutions shared by the community often involve using the phone number alongside an email address for authentication. I’m planning to use ERPNext in India, where most people are mobile-first rather than email-first. A native way to let users - including my staff, customers, and vendors - authenticate using just their phone number and OTP would offer a much better experience than requiring an email address first and then optionally adding a phone number later. Here are a few discussions I found that didn’t quite provide the solution I was looking for: Here are a few discussions I found without the answer I was looking for How to make the user sign up with mobile number instead of email In this discussion, the suggested solution is to enable “Allow Login using Mobile Number” in the settings. However, this only allows users to use their mobile number at the login step and does not eliminate the requirement to have an email address to begin with. Login with Mobile and OTP Here the solution is to use a custom whitelisted function (code provided at agrinext/agrinext/otp.py at develop · agrinext/agrinext · GitHub ) which can authenticate using phone + OTP. But this still needs the user to have a valid email address to create the account. Is there a better solution?

title: Can Anyone Help Me Create a Product Bundle in ERPNext?
first_post: Hi Everyone, I’m trying to create a product bundle in ERPNext. Example: Laptop + Mouse + Bag sold together as one package. I’m not sure about the correct setup How to link the items into one bundle Whether the price is taken from the child items or set manually If I can change bundle contents for a specific order Can anyone guide me step-by-step? Thanks in advance!
full_text: Hi Everyone, I’m trying to create a product bundle in ERPNext. Example: Laptop + Mouse + Bag sold together as one package. I’m not sure about the correct setup How to link the items into one bundle Whether the price is taken from the child items or set manually If I can change bundle contents for a specific order Can anyone guide me step-by-step? Thanks in advance! Hi @Petergrge Please consult with documentation; https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/product-bundle Petergrge: Hi Everyone, I’m trying to create a product bundle in ERPNext. Example: Laptop + Mouse + Bag sold together as one package. I’m not sure about the correct setup How to link the items into one bundle Whether the price is taken from the child items or set manually If I can change bundle contents for a specific order Can anyone guide me step-by-step? Thanks in advance! Hi @Petergrge Nice — bundling laptop + mouse + bag is a very common use-case in ERPNext. Below I’ll give a clear, production-safe step-by-step: how to create the bundle, how price is decided, what you can (and shouldn’t) change per order, and a couple of alternative approaches if you need stock for the parent item. I’ll cite the official docs for the key bits. ( Product Bundle ) Quick summary Use Product Bundle (a sales-side BOM) and a non-stock Parent Item . Child items are the actual shippable stock items. Frappe Documentation The parent’s selling price is the one fetched for the bundle in sales transactions (you can manage it via Product Bundle master or regular Item Price/Price List rules). Frappe Documentation When you add the parent to a Sales Order/Invoice/Delivery Note, ERPNext explodes the bundle into the Packing List (editable for warehouse/serial/batch); on submit, stock of child items is reduced. ( Sales Order ) Step-by-step (Laptop + Mouse + Bag) Create the child Items (if not already): Laptop , Mouse , Bag . These are stock items with Maintain Stock = Yes . Create a Parent Item that represents the bundle (e.g., LAPTOP-BUNDLE-01 ). For this Parent Item set Maintain Stock = No (it’s a virtual item). Docs: Parent must be a non-stock item. Frappe Documentation Go to: Home → Selling → Items and Pricing → Product Bundle → New . Select the Parent Item . Add child rows: Laptop qty 1, Mouse qty 1, Bag qty 1. Enter the bundle price to be used when selling (the Product Bundle screen allows specifying the parent price). Save. Frappe Documentation Create a Sales Order or Sales Invoice and add LAPTOP-BUNDLE-01 as the line item. When you save the transaction, ERPNext will populate the Packing List with the 3 child items and their quantities. You’ll be asked to select a Delivery Warehouse and can edit warehouse/serial/batch in Packing List. On submission, ERPNext will deduct stock of the child items from the chosen warehouse(s). ( Sales Order ) Pricing: where does the price come from? The Product Bundle master stores a price for the parent which is fetched in sales transactions. Use that field or manage prices through Item Price / Price List if you need price lists or channel-specific prices. (Docs show price for parent is fetched.) Frappe Documentation Can I change bundle contents for a specific order? You can edit the Packing List generated for the order: change the Warehouse, Serial No, Batch, and quantities for packing/fulfilment. This is the supported place to make fulfillment-level adjustments. Frappe Documentation Replacing a child SKU with a completely different SKU is technically possible (by editing the Packing List rows), but: it breaks the link back to the defined Product Bundle and may confuse reporting/automation, downstream documents (Purchase Order generation, fulfilment logic) might expect the original children, it’s not the “official” way to offer configurable bundles. Recommended approaches if bundle needs to be customized often: Create multiple Product Bundles (variants) for common configurations (e.g., LAPTOP-BUNDLE-SSD-512 , LAPTOP-BUNDLE-SSD-1TB ). Use Sales BOM / Manufacturing + Repack if you want the bundle to be a stock item (see below). Use a small customization (client script or server hook) to allow selecting options on Sales Order and auto-replace child items in Packing List before save/submit. There’s been community discussion requesting more advanced configurable bundle behavior — ERPNext’s out-of-the-box support focuses on fixed bundles + editable packing list for fulfilment tweaks. GitHub If you want the Parent to be a stock item (assemble into stock) If you need to maintain stock for the Parent Item (i.e., you want a stock SKU for the bundle), use a regular BOM and do a Stock Entry → Repack (package components into the finished bundle). The docs recommend BOM + Stock Entry for that workflow. This gives you inventory for the parent and normal manufacturing accounting. Frappe Documentation Practical tips / Best practices Keep parent as non-stock unless you have to show the bundle as an inventory SKU. Non-stock parent + Product Bundle is simpler for offers and quick selling. Frappe Documentation Manage prices centrally via Price Lists so you can change bundle selling price without editing the bundle master each time. If you plan to let salespeople customize bundles a lot, consider creating a simple UI (client script) that presents common options and builds the correct Product Bundle/packing list programmatically. Test end-to-end: Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice → check Stock Ledger to confirm child stock reduction. Thanks

title: How to Handle Partial Delivery from Supplier in ERPNext?
first_post: Hello everyone, I’m facing an issue where my supplier only delivered 20 units out of a 30-unit purchase order. My customer, however, received the 20 units. What is the standard procedure to handle this in ERPNext? I have a few options in mind: How can I process a credit note to the supplier for the 10 missing units? How can I manage the Sales Invoice to my customer if they only paid for the 20 units they received? What’s the best way to handle this on the Purchase Invoice side? Thank you for your help.
full_text: Hello everyone, I’m facing an issue where my supplier only delivered 20 units out of a 30-unit purchase order. My customer, however, received the 20 units. What is the standard procedure to handle this in ERPNext? I have a few options in mind: How can I process a credit note to the supplier for the 10 missing units? How can I manage the Sales Invoice to my customer if they only paid for the 20 units they received? What’s the best way to handle this on the Purchase Invoice side? Thank you for your help. Hi, Answer to your questions solely depends on the Local Compliance Rule. In Ideal Scenario you will Issue Debit Note to the Supplier and Not Credit Note. Also, this needs to be done if the vendor has billed you for 30 qty and delivered only 20, If billing is for 20qty no need of issuing Debit Note. From the Customer Perspective, You just have to issue a sales Invoice for the qty you are delivering This is a common situation, and ERPNext has ways to handle it smoothly. Here’s how you can manage each part: Credit Note to Supplier for Missing 10 Units: Since your supplier delivered only 20 out of 30 units, you can create a Purchase Return or a Credit Note against the supplier’s Purchase Invoice for the 10 undelivered units. Alternatively, you can update the Purchase Receipt to reflect only the 20 units received, so your Purchase Invoice will be based on that quantity. Then raise a Credit Note or request a refund/adjustment for the missing units. Sales Invoice for Customer Paying Only for 20 Units: Your Sales Invoice should match what the customer actually received — so invoice for 20 units only. If you initially created an invoice for 30 units, you can create a Sales Return or issue a Credit Note for the 10 units not delivered. Make sure your delivery note and invoice quantities are aligned. Handling Purchase Invoice: The Purchase Invoice should be based on the goods actually received (20 units). If you already created an invoice for 30 units, you can submit a Purchase Invoice Return or Credit Note for the 10 missing units. Otherwise, only create the Purchase Invoice for the 20 units you have received. Please check out the below video for more details. Thank you so much, I do familiar with these. I will watch and apply this first. dormant: I’m facing an issue where my supplier only delivered 20 units out of a 30-unit purchase order. My customer, however, received the 20 units. What is the standard procedure to handle this in ERPNext? I have a few options in mind: How can I process a credit note to the supplier for the 10 missing units? How can I manage the Sales Invoice to my customer if they only paid for the 20 units they received? What’s the best way to handle this on the Purchase Invoice side? Thank you for your help. Hi Dormant Okay — in ERPNext this scenario is basically a partial delivery situation, and you want to keep all three sides correct: Purchasing side (supplier only delivered 20 of 30) Sales side (customer only got 20 of 30) Accounts side (credit note for supplier, invoice adjustment for customer) Here’s how you can handle it cleanly without breaking traceability. 1. On the Purchase Side (Supplier → You) Option A – Bill Only for What You Received (Preferred) When you create the Purchase Receipt , receive 20 units instead of 30. Then create the Purchase Invoice from the Purchase Receipt so it only picks up 20 units. The remaining 10 units on the Purchase Order will stay as “Pending” in status. If the supplier never sends the remaining 10 units, close the Purchase Order so they’re not expected anymore. Option B – Already Invoiced for 30 Units? If you already booked a Purchase Invoice for 30: Create a Purchase Return for the missing 10 units (against that invoice). This generates a Credit Note (Purchase Return Invoice) automatically in ERPNext. It reduces the payable amount to the supplier. Link that credit note to the supplier payment or keep it as credit for future orders. 2. On the Sales Side (You → Customer) If Customer Only Received 20 Units: Deliver 20 units in the Delivery Note . When you make the Sales Invoice from the Delivery Note, it will bill only for 20 units. The Sales Order will still show 10 units pending. If you won’t be delivering the rest, update the Sales Order and mark the remaining items as Closed . If You Already Invoiced for 30 Units: Create a Sales Return for 10 units (which weren’t delivered) against the Sales Invoice. ERPNext will create a Credit Note (Sales Return Invoice) for the customer. You can either refund or adjust in the next invoice. 3. Accounting Impact Purchase Return → decreases expenses / reduces accounts payable to supplier. Sales Return → decreases sales revenue / reduces accounts receivable from customer. Both sides stay balanced, and you keep a proper audit trail. Example Workflow – Recommended Purchase Order: 30 units. Purchase Receipt: 20 units. Purchase Invoice (from receipt): 20 units. Delivery Note to customer: 20 units. Sales Invoice (from delivery note): 20 units. Close remaining quantities in both PO and SO if no further delivery will happen. Pro tip: ERPNext’s “Billing %” and “Delivered Qty” columns on PO/SO will help you track exactly how much remains outstanding. title: Defered JV belongs to Purchase Invoive
first_post: Does ERPNext’s scheduler create automatic backdated entries (JV) for deferred expenses? For example, if the invoice service start date is 1 Jan 2025 and the end date is 30 Jun 2025, and I create purchase invoice today (1 Aug 2025).
full_text: Does ERPNext’s scheduler create automatic backdated entries (JV) for deferred expenses? For example, if the invoice service start date is 1 Jan 2025 and the end date is 30 Jun 2025, and I create purchase invoice today (1 Aug 2025). No — ERPNext’s deferred accounting will not create backdated Journal Entries automatically. Here’s why: The Deferred Expense (or Deferred Revenue ) feature works by spreading the expense/revenue over the defined service period starting from the posting date forward . The scheduler job ( process_deferred_accounting ) runs daily and looks at future recognition dates, not past ones. If you post a Purchase Invoice on 1 Aug 2025 with a service start date of 1 Jan 2025 , ERPNext won’t automatically go back and create JVs for Jan–Jul 2025. Instead, it will: Create the first recognition entry on the next scheduler run after your posting date. Recognize the remaining deferred amount over the remaining period only. If you want Jan–Jul to be recognized: You’ll need to manually create catch-up JVs for the past months. Or, adjust the deferred schedule manually in Invoice → Deferred Expense/Revenue child table before running the scheduler. Pro tip: If you need ERPNext to create all missed months automatically, you’d have to customize process_deferred_accounting to: Detect missed periods based on service start date Post backdated JVs But you need to be careful — backdated entries can affect closed accounting periods. title: About BOM Template.
first_post: I have set an Item template on BOM Finished goods field and another item template over Raw material field. When I am going to create the Work order, how should I consume the varients of the set Item template on Raw material field.
full_text: I have set an Item template on BOM Finished goods field and another item template over Raw material field. When I am going to create the Work order, how should I consume the varients of the set Item template on Raw material field. In ERPNext, if you set Item Templates (i.e., “Template Items” with variants) in the BOM for raw materials, the system will not automatically pick a specific variant when you create a Work Order — it will use exactly the Item Code you’ve set in the BOM. That means if your BOM says RAW-TEMPLATE and that’s a template (non-stock) item, the Work Order will not know which variant (e.g., RAW-TEMPLATE-RED , RAW-TEMPLATE-BLUE ) to consume unless you explicitly tell it. How to handle raw material variants in a Work Order Here are the common approaches: 1. Create BOMs for each variant Create one BOM per finished goods variant, and set the raw materials as the exact variants to be used. Example: BOM for FG-RED → raw material RAW-TEMPLATE-RED BOM for FG-BLUE → raw material RAW-TEMPLATE-BLUE Pros: No confusion during production; fully automated. Cons: More BOM records to maintain. 2. Use “Update Raw Materials” in the Work Order Keep the BOM linked to the template item for raw materials. After creating the Work Order, go to the Raw Materials table and manually change the template item to the specific variant you are consuming. This works if the variant choice is made just before production. Pros: Single BOM. Cons: Manual step every time. 3. Custom Script for Variant Selection Add a Custom Field in the Work Order to select a raw material variant (e.g., Color, Size). Use a Client Script or Server Script to replace the template item in the Work Order’s raw materials table with the selected variant before submission. Pros: Keeps BOM maintenance minimal and ensures correct stock deduction. Cons: Requires scripting knowledge. 4. Use “Attribute-driven BOM selection” (Custom Feature) ERPNext doesn’t natively do attribute-based raw material substitution, but you can: Write a small app or hook on the before_submit of Work Order. Pull the correct variant based on Finished Goods variant attributes. This way, raw material variants are automatically matched. Important: If your BOM uses a template item and you don’t replace it with an actual stock variant before manufacturing, ERPNext will not be able to reserve or consume stock because template items are not stock items.

Below my setup do i missing anything? image 474×121 6.21 KB image 1089×1296 87.1 KB image 1092×544 40 KB image 1146×429 33.8 KB image 1097×431 33.7 KB image 1027×458 52.3 KB Hello everyone, Voltass: I am having a little problem on purchase invoice. I have a two VAT on one invoice 7% and 0% but after set it from tutorial about taxes on youtube from Frappe on submit get error " Tax should be 7.0% of the base amount Note: To correct base amount, fill in Tax Base Amount." Hi Voltass Please try the following either should work. Method 1: Use “Tax Category” per item Go to your taxable items (7%) in the invoice and set Item Tax Template with 7% VAT. For zero-rated items (0%), set Item Tax Template with 0% VAT. In the Taxes table, make sure Charge Type = “On Net Total” and Based On = “Item Tax Template”. Remove any extra “Tax Base Amount” you typed in — let ERPNext calculate it. Save & Submit. Method 2: Adjust “Tax Base Amount” manually If you want to keep both VATs in the same invoice without templates: In the Taxes table, for the 7% VAT row, set Tax Base Amount = sum of base amounts of only those items that are taxable at 7%. For the 0% VAT row, set Tax Base Amount = sum of base amounts of items that are zero-rated. Make sure Tax Amount is exactly Base Amount × 7% for the 7% row. Extra checks Ensure “Validate Tax Amount” setting in your Purchase Invoice DocType isn’t too strict. If you want some tolerance, go to: Accounts Settings → Tax Calculation Rounding and adjust. Check that Item Tax Template matches Purchase Taxes and Charges Template . I use v15 version there is no option to select Based On or Tax Base Amount to set Right — in Frappe/ERPNext v15 , the “Based On” and “Tax Base Amount” fields you’ve seen in older tutorials no longer appear in the default Purchase Taxes and Charges UI. ERPNext now automatically calculates the tax base amount from: The items linked to the tax via Item Tax Template The “Charge Type” and “Included In Print Rate” settings The “Applicable On” (Net Total / Valuation / Total) field So the fix for your two VAT rates (7% & 0%) problem in v15 is a bit different than in older versions. How to do it in ERPNext v15 without Tax Base Amount field 1. Create two Item Tax Templates Go to: Accounts → Item Tax Template → New Name: VAT 7% Tax Type: VAT Tax Rate: 7.0 Save. Create another template: VAT 0% Tax Type: VAT Tax Rate: 0.0 2. Assign the right tax template to items Open each item in your Purchase Invoice and set the Item Tax Template : Items with 7% VAT → VAT 7% template Items with 0% VAT → VAT 0% template 3. Set up Purchase Taxes and Charges Template Go to: Accounts → Purchase Taxes and Charges Template → New Add a row: Type : On Net Total Account Head : VAT Payable Rate : 7.0 Save. (You don’t need to add 0% VAT here; ERPNext will calculate it as zero based on the template.) 4. Use the template in your Purchase Invoice In the Purchase Invoice, select your Purchase Taxes and Charges Template . ERPNext will: Apply 7% VAT to items with the 7% template. Apply 0% VAT to zero-rated items. title: How to Manage Department-Wise Expense Limits in Frappe?
first_post: We want to set monthly or quarterly expense limits for each department (e.g., Marketing, Sales, IT) and track employee spending against those limits. Ideally, the system should: Tag Expense Claims to the correct department Alert department heads when spending is near the limit Stop or escalate claims that go over budget We’re using Cost Centers and Budgets, but it’s not clear how to enforce these controls automatically.
full_text: We want to set monthly or quarterly expense limits for each department (e.g., Marketing, Sales, IT) and track employee spending against those limits. Ideally, the system should: Tag Expense Claims to the correct department Alert department heads when spending is near the limit Stop or escalate claims that go over budget We’re using Cost Centers and Budgets, but it’s not clear how to enforce these controls automatically. Hi @JitenDhabhi1354 You can make Department doctype as Accounting Dimension and then set Budget against each Department and the Budgeted Amount can be distributed as per your requirements on Monthly basis by defining Monthly Distribution within Budget docytpe as well. Knowing the fact Budgets are defined against GL Accounts within a Fiscal Year and in your particular use case , the Recording Phase takes effect provided GL Accounts, Department and fiscal year matches. The Most of the recording elements are itemized where you have to pick and choose items (stock items, service items and Assets) in different docytpes child tables and you have to make sure correct GL Account with rest of the dimension are linked so that budget can play its part. Due to Itemized nature of the ERP, Item Manager (Role) has to be someone within house as a super user to control accounting elements based on items so that any other user on Basic Recording phase should not change those settings and each expense record should go under respective department budget with its defaults. The Role Permission Manager and User Permissions are where you should control Basic Recording levels and make sure each user should follow correct expense recordings. The Notification Module will help triggering notification on any event during recording phases of expense under budgets. The Auto email report can help manager to be notified existing or remaining limit on their budget periodically. This is how Budget takes effect and play its part effectively.

title: Sales invoices not emailing customers after upgrade — emails stuck in queue
first_post: Hi everyone, I’m facing a problem after upgrading our ERPNext server. When we submit a Sales Invoice, the system says the email is queued, but the customer never receives it. The Email Queue keeps growing, and the status stays as “Not Sent.” If I click “Send Now,” nothing changes. Sometimes it works right after a server restart, but stops again after a while. Our setup: ERPNext v14, Ubuntu server, production setup Using Gmail/Google Workspace SMTP (App Password) No custom code related to email How do I properly clear the stuck emails and get the queue moving again? What logs or screens should I check to find the real error?
full_text: Hi everyone, I’m facing a problem after upgrading our ERPNext server. When we submit a Sales Invoice, the system says the email is queued, but the customer never receives it. The Email Queue keeps growing, and the status stays as “Not Sent.” If I click “Send Now,” nothing changes. Sometimes it works right after a server restart, but stops again after a while. Our setup: ERPNext v14, Ubuntu server, production setup Using Gmail/Google Workspace SMTP (App Password) No custom code related to email How do I properly clear the stuck emails and get the queue moving again? What logs or screens should I check to find the real error? Check if Frappe worker processes are running sudo supervisorctl status If worker processes are stopped or restarting frequently , email sending won’t work. To restart workers: cd ~/frappe-bench bench restart Check Email Logs ERPNext logs email sending errors in: # For bench logs cd ~/frappe-bench bench --site your-site-name console Or directly check the logs: # Worker logs tail -f logs/worker.error.log # Scheduler logs (sometimes relevant) tail -f logs/scheduler.error.log Clear Stuck Emails If you want to reset the queue , you have two options: Option A — Retry individual emails Go to Email Queue → select emails → Send Now Option B — Clear the queue entirely cd ~/frappe-bench bench --site your-site-name execute frappe.email.queue.clear This removes unsent emails — use only if you are okay losing queued emails. Check Scheduler ERPNext sends some emails via scheduler events . Make sure the scheduler is running: bench --site your-site-name doctor It will tell you if Redis, Workers, or Scheduler is misconfigured. You can start a worker in foreground to see why emails fail: bench worker

Key points: When creating or editing a document (like a Sales Order , Item , or a custom DocType), the Attach File / Attach Image field allows direct camera capture . The salesperson can take a photo on the spot, and it will be uploaded to ERPNext immediately. No extra coding required; works offline and syncs when online. Recommended for: Quick deployment, minimal setup, real-time upload. 2. Custom Web Form with Camera Upload If you want the sales team to use a mobile browser instead of the app: Create a Web Form in ERPNext for the DocType where photos are needed. Add a File / Attach Image field . Modern mobile browsers will allow “Take Photo” directly from the camera when attaching. Steps: Go to the DocType → Web Form → Add the fields you want. Ensure the Attach Image / File field is included. Share the link with salespeople; they can open it on mobile, take a photo, and submit. Recommended for: Teams that don’t want to install the ERPNext app. 3. Use a Custom Mobile Integration (Optional) If you need extra automation , e.g., auto-tagging photos with location, creating documents automatically, you can build a custom mobile app or Frappe REST API integration . This requires developer effort but gives full control. title: How to Record Promissory Notes / Security Documents as Off-Balance Sheet in ERPNext?
first_post: Hi everyone, I’m looking for guidance on how to properly record and track security documents—such as promissory notes, checks held as guarantee, or similar instruments—in ERPNext. These documents are purely for control purposes and do not represent actual assets or liabilities in the balance sheet, nor should they affect the Profit & Loss statement. Specifically, I’m seeking advice on: How to set up a control (off-balance sheet) account in ERPNext for promissory notes or security documents—should it be created under a specific Root Type (e.g. Liability) with a certain Account Type (e.g. Payable or Temporary)?
full_text: Hi everyone, I’m looking for guidance on how to properly record and track security documents—such as promissory notes, checks held as guarantee, or similar instruments—in ERPNext. These documents are purely for control purposes and do not represent actual assets or liabilities in the balance sheet, nor should they affect the Profit & Loss statement. Specifically, I’m seeking advice on: How to set up a control (off-balance sheet) account in ERPNext for promissory notes or security documents—should it be created under a specific Root Type (e.g. Liability) with a certain Account Type (e.g. Payable or Temporary)? Hi @sfarbod You should try Bank Guarantee doctype as it does not impact GL and can serve the purpose of Promissory Note. https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/bank-guarantee ERPNext Handles This; Out-of-the-box, ERPNext records and tracks BGs but does not automatically hit the GL except for margin money and bank charges . You can link BGs to Sales Orders / Purchase Orders for better contract compliance. Further talking about GL Accounts under Chart of Accounts, account type of each one infact determines the behavior of how the GL is going to be reacting during Recording Phase. Since there is no GL hit as far as BG is concerned, To reflect Temporary liabilities, some companies create a custom account group “Contingent Liabilities” and manually book entries if they want it visible in reports. Apart from all above, the Payment Request can also help communicate or chase payments based on Invoices as well. Hi @ahsantareen , Thank you very much for your clear explanation and for pointing me towards the Bank Guarantee doctype —this seems to cover a good part of my requirement. One additional point: since for my case the movement of security documents (e.g., when receiving or returning promissory notes) is important to track, I would also like to define a control account (contingent account) just to monitor turnovers, without impacting the Balance Sheet or P&L. From your experience, what would be the best practice to set this up in ERPNext? Should I create a custom account group such as “Contingent Liabilities” (under Liability root type) and then use that for manual entries, or would you suggest a different approach for handling these purely off-balance-sheet records? Thanks again for your helpful guidance @sfarbod You can rename Bank Gurantee doctype as Promissory Note / Security Document as per your likings. Making this docytpe Accounting Dimension will also help you to tag all your JVs with respective Notes and all accounting / Financial Reports will have a filter for better reporting. Generally a temporary Liability account serve the purpose of Provisions efficiently.

So: What’s the porpouse of the “allowed modules” section in the user’s ‘roles and permissions’ tab? @Prytesh according to you, that means you are required to change ERPNext’ workspaces definition to avoid certain users to have the links shown in the side bar? Exactly The “Allowed Modules” section in the User doctype is legacy — it used to control which modules appeared in the sidebar. On current develop branch , it no longer hides or restricts access by itself. Roles → control CRUD permissions on DocTypes. Allowed Modules → only a UI preference (whether a module shortcut used to be shown). It doesn’t override roles. Workspaces → now drive what shows in the sidebar. Each workspace can be restricted to certain roles. So yes: if you want to prevent users from seeing certain links in the sidebar, you should adjust the Workspace definitions (set role restrictions there). The “Allowed Modules” checkboxes don’t enforce this anymore. Ok, so after playing around… @Prytesh mentioned: Workspaces → now drive what shows in the sidebar. Each workspace can be restricted to certain roles." Is it possible the other way around? I.e. specifying the roles the workspace should be hidden for? I ask this because, right now, erpnext (dev) workspaces definition doesn’t include any role in them, so I assume workspaces are shown based on the doctype access links inside the workspace.

title: How can I handle a Purchase Rate Adjustment?
first_post: How can I handle a Purchase Rate Adjustment ? For example, I booked a Purchase Invoice at a certain rate, but later the supplier sent a revised invoice with a lower/higher item rate. Should I use a Debit Note, Landed Cost Voucher, or a Journal Entry for this kind of adjustment? I want to make sure both the supplier ledger and the stock valuation remain correct. What’s the best practice in this case?
full_text: How can I handle a Purchase Rate Adjustment ? For example, I booked a Purchase Invoice at a certain rate, but later the supplier sent a revised invoice with a lower/higher item rate. Should I use a Debit Note, Landed Cost Voucher, or a Journal Entry for this kind of adjustment? I want to make sure both the supplier ledger and the stock valuation remain correct. What’s the best practice in this case? @Astha-pandit Use Purchase Return / Debit Note if the supplier issues a revised invoice — this keeps both supplier ledger and stock valuation correct. If stock rate changes after posting → use Landed Cost Voucher to adjust stock valuation. If it’s only a price correction, not stock impact → a Debit/Credit Note is the clean way. @Astha-pandit Hello if the supplier revises the invoice, create a Debit Note against the original to keep the supplier ledger correct. If the change affects stock valuation (like freight or rate correction), use a Landed Cost Voucher.

title: Consider process loss checkbox
first_post: What does consider process loss checkbox in workorder exactly do image 1387×476 36.1 KB
full_text: What does consider process loss checkbox in workorder exactly do image 1387×476 36.1 KB DakshKothari18: What does consider process loss checkbox in workorder exactly do @DakshKothari18 The “Consider Process Loss” checkbox in a Work Order is used when your production process naturally results in a loss of raw materials (wastage, evaporation, scrap, etc.). Here’s what it does exactly: When checked, ERPNext looks at the Process Loss % (defined in the BOM or operation) while issuing raw materials. The system will then increase the required raw material qty so that after accounting for the expected loss, you still produce the intended finished goods qty. Example: You want to make 100 kg of Product. BOM shows it needs 100 kg of raw material with 5% process loss . If “Consider Process Loss” is checked → system will reserve/issue 105 kg of raw material (100 usable + 5 lost). In short: Checked = raw material requirement accounts for process loss. Unchecked = system assumes zero process loss, only reserves exact qty as per BOM.

title: Weldments import Uom
first_post: Good day I’m busy setting up a company and busy adding items. How do you guys import weldments? For those that don’t know, weldments are metal extrusions like tubing or angle irons. What I want to do is ,import the weldments as a full length (6000mm and 13000mm) and then when manufacturing consume from a full length. The rest must go to scrap. I’m not sure where or what to do.
full_text: Good day I’m busy setting up a company and busy adding items. How do you guys import weldments? For those that don’t know, weldments are metal extrusions like tubing or angle irons. What I want to do is ,import the weldments as a full length (6000mm and 13000mm) and then when manufacturing consume from a full length. The rest must go to scrap. I’m not sure where or what to do. Good day, This is a classic manufacturing inventory problem, and ERPNext handles it very well using its Unit of Measure (UoM) conversion features. Here’s a step-by-step guide to achieve exactly what you need. The core idea is to stock your weldments in the unit you purchase them in (e.g., “Length”) but consume them in a smaller unit (e.g., “mm”) in your Bill of Materials (BOM). Step 1: Set Up Your Units of Measure (UoM) First, we need to make sure the system understands the relationship between a full length and millimeters. Go to the Unit of Measure List . Ensure you have a base UoM like “mm” (Millimeter). Create a new UoM for your full lengths. Let’s call it “Length 6m” for your 6000mm pieces. Now, create a UoM Conversion Factor . This is the most important step. Go to the UoM Conversion List and click “Add UoM Conversion”. UOM: Length 6m Conversion Factor: 6000 UOM: mm This tells the system that 1 “Length 6m” = 6000 “mm” .Repeat this for your 13000mm lengths (e.g., create a “Length 13m” UoM with a conversion factor of 13000). Step 2: Create Your Weldment Item Now, let’s set up the Angle Iron item itself. Go to the Item List and create a new Item (e.g., “Angle Iron 50x50”). Make sure it is a Stock Item . In the “UNITS OF MEASURE” section, set the Stock UOM to Length 6m . This is the unit you will use for purchasing and for your main stock balance. In the “UOMs” table below, add a new row for mm . The conversion factor (6000) will be automatically fetched from the setup in Step 1. Your item is now set up to be stocked in full lengths but can be transacted in millimeters. Step 3: Configure the Bill of Materials (BOM) This is where you define how much material is consumed during manufacturing. Create a BOM for the finished product you are manufacturing. In the “Raw Materials” table, add your “Angle Iron 50x50” item. In that row, change the UOM from the default (“Length 6m”) to “mm” . Enter the exact quantity in millimeters required for one unit of your finished product. For example, if you need a 1.5-meter piece, you would enter 1500 in the Qty field. When you save the BOM, the system now knows that to produce one finished good, it needs to consume 1500 mm of Angle Iron. Step 4: The Manufacturing Process & Handling Scrap This is where everything comes together. Create a Work Order for your finished product. The required quantity of Angle Iron will be automatically calculated in mm. When you create a Stock Entry (Material Transfer for Manufacturing) from the Work Order, the system will request 1500 mm from your stores. Since your stock is kept in “Length 6m”, the system will automatically deduct 0.25 of a “Length 6m” from your inventory (because 1500 / 6000 = 0.25). Your stock level will correctly show, for example, 9.75 “Length 6m” remaining. How to handle the scrap (the remaining 4500mm): The simplest and most common accounting practice is to let the cost of the entire raw material (the full 6000mm length) be absorbed into the manufacturing cost of the finished product. In this scenario, you don’t need to do anything else in the system. The system has already deducted the material value from inventory and added it to the Work-in-Progress warehouse. The physical 4500mm off-cut is simply treated as scrap. This is the most straightforward way and is correct from a costing perspective, as the cost of that scrap is part of the production cost. If your scrap has a very high value and you need to track it as a separate inventory item, you could explore using “By-Products” in the BOM, but for most weldment operations, the method described above is the standard and recommended approach. Hope this helps you get set up! Please let me know if you have any questions or need assistance applying this. Best regards, Tharun Kumar K +91 6381360779

title: How to get stock balance having inventory dimension in server script?
first_post: x = frappe.call('erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001', warehouse='Finished Goods - T' ) print(x) output: 1471.0 with inventory dimension: x = frappe.call('erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001', warehouse='Finished Goods - T', inventory_dimensions_dict={'customer': 'test'} ) print(x) output: 1471.0
full_text: x = frappe.call('erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001', warehouse='Finished Goods - T' ) print(x) output: 1471.0 with inventory dimension: x = frappe.call('erpnext.stock.utils.get_stock_balance', item_code='STO-ITEM-2025-00001', warehouse='Finished Goods - T', inventory_dimensions_dict={'customer': 'test'} ) print(x) output: 1471.0 Actually, I noticed that get_stock_balance does not handle inventory dimensions correctly. It simply fetches the qty_after_transaction from the Stock Ledger Entry, which is why you are still seeing 1471.0 even after passing the inventory dimension. FE If you make a Stock Entry for Item A with a quantity of 1000 in Warehouse B , the SLE will show Qty Change = 1000 and Qty After Transaction = 1000 . Then, if you make another entry for the same item and warehouse but with an inventory dimension (say, Customer C ) and a quantity of 471 , the new SLE will show Qty Change = 471 and Qty After Transaction = 1471 . This is why get_stock_balance always returns 1471.0, as it does not filter by the inventory dimension. Are you sure? In my most recent testing I found that it now does at least return dimensioned quantity correctly, but there is no way to get undimensioned quantity. Can you post a video or screenshot? Also, I found that the Inventory Dimension Validation Logic doesn’t make sense, and I can’t fix it because there is no function that returns undimensioned stock of an item. What I mean is that when you create a material receipt with qty 100 of item1 with dimension x and after that create a material issue for qty 50 of item1 without dimension, the system will not throw a validation error saying there is no undimensioned stock. Instead, it does some very weird thing where undimensioned stock of item1 is now -50 (even though negative stock is disabled) and dimensioned stock remains 100. I have contacted Support multiple times about this, but they claim it works as intended because -50 + 100 = 50, lmao. By the way, this behavior causes another issue where sometimes 0-stock items show up in the balance report because the valuation rate somehow becomes negative. Again, this is with default settings. In short, Inventory Dimension is basically unusable this way. The only workaround is to make the dimension mandatory, but this limits the flexibility of the feature a lot. My suggestion would be to develop Inventory Dimensions further so they are part of the Bin doctype (I even offered to pay for the feature) or at least validate undimensioned stock correctly if that is too large of a change. Nevermind my last answer it still does not return the correct qty. When testing this i made the mistake to not check for multiple consecutive stock entries with different dimension values which caused exactly the one i checked to accidentally be correct because it was the first stock entry and for that item/dimension value combination stock never left inventory after that. Bottom line is it returns the wrong qty, i wrote some utility functions that actually return the correct qty in my custom app, if someone needs it hit me up.

first_post: Hello All, I have a question regarding valuation rate - when I create a landed cost voucher, the valuation rate for that item changes. Is there a way to change the valuation rate across all warehouse for that item (old stock as well) once a landed cost voucher is created?
full_text: Hello All, I have a question regarding valuation rate - when I create a landed cost voucher, the valuation rate for that item changes. And if the item already exists in that warehouse, the existing item valuation rate will not change, only newly entered ones. Is there a way to change the valuation rate across all warehouse for that item (old stock as well) once a landed cost voucher is created? title: Pick List Barcode Scanning broken in v15.76.0
first_post: We are on the latest ERPNext (v15.76.0) and noticed that barcode scanning in the Pick List no longer works . This workflow has always worked fine for us in previous versions (we update regularly and were on v15.74 before). Barcode scanning still works correctly in all other documents (Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry, Transfer, etc.) – only the Pick List is affected. Since our warehouse operations rely heavily on scanning items into Pick Lists on a daily basis, this issue is a serious blocker for us. Thanks.
full_text: We are on the latest ERPNext (v15.76.0) and noticed that barcode scanning in the Pick List no longer works . This workflow has always worked fine for us in previous versions (we update regularly and were on v15.74 before). Barcode scanning still works correctly in all other documents (Purchase Receipt, Delivery Note, Stock Entry, Transfer, etc.) – only the Pick List is affected. Since our warehouse operations rely heavily on scanning items into Pick Lists on a daily basis, this issue is a serious blocker for us. Thanks. The root cause of this bug is a logic change in the get_row_to_modify_on_scan function within the core utility file: erpnext/public/js/utils/barcode_scanner.js. A new, stricter warehouse_match condition was introduced. The bug is in the else block of this new logic: // From the new, code let warehouse_match = true; if (has_warehouse_field) { if (warehouse) { warehouse_match = row[warehouse_field] === warehouse; } else { // THIS IS THE BUG! warehouse_match = !row[warehouse_field]; } } This code is executed when no specific warehouse has been scanned beforehand, which is the standard procedure for a Pick List. The line warehouse_match = !row[warehouse_field]; incorrectly requires the warehouse field in the item row to be empty to get a match. In a Pick List, every item row always has a warehouse assigned. Therefore, row[warehouse_field] is never empty, the condition !row[warehouse_field] is always false, the warehouse_match fails, and the scanner never finds a valid row to update. The change seems to be part of a feature: feat: enhance barcode scanner to support warehouse scanning (#48865) · frappe/erpnext@227fadc · GitHub Could this lead you to a workaround? I didn’t check if this is linked to some updated documentation regarding scanning, which might help to adapt to the changed workflow ( if this is not considered as a bug by the dev). Hi Peer, Thanks for finding the original PR! That’s very helpful. You are right that the change is part of a new feature. However, this feature introduces a critical regression for the Pick List workflow. In a Pick List, every item row is already assigned to a specific warehouse. The new logic ( warehouse_match = !row[warehouse_field]; ) incorrectly assumes the warehouse field might be empty and fails every time because it’s always filled. This makes it impossible to scan any item. Forcing users to scan a warehouse before every item in a Pick List would be a major step back in usability. Therefore, this is a bug caused by an unintended side effect of the new feature. The change in my Pull Request fix(stock): Correct warehouse matching in barcode scanner by maydo7777 · Pull Request #49294 · frappe/erpnext · GitHub corrects this specific issue for the Pick List workflow while leaving the new “warehouse-first scanning” feature intact for other documents where it makes sense. Hi, This seems like a genuine bug. Sorry for the oversight on our side. The fix proposed by @maydo7777 will break some of our designs though. I will attempt the proper fix. Fixed in fix: multiple fixes to warehouse barcode scanning logic by sagarvora · Pull Request #49312 · frappe/erpnext · GitHub @snv ThankYou

full_text: I want to update certain apps not all my apps this command bench update or bench update --reset updating all apps i have i want to update one of them only Is there a way to do it ? just navigate to the desired app directory: cd /frappe-bench/apps/erpnext then do git pull This would pull the latest updates for that specific app After that, just migrate all your sites to get the updated app features. Thanks Hi @Mohemd_Ali : You can use bench update --apps yourapp Additionally: Options: --pull Pull updates for all the apps in bench --apps TEXT --patch Run migrations for all sites in the bench --build Build JS and CSS assets for the bench --requirements Update requirements. If run alone, equivalent to `bench setup requirements` --restart-supervisor Restart supervisor processes after update --restart-systemd Restart systemd units after update --no-backup If this flag is set, sites won't be backed up prior to updates. Note: This is not recommended in production. --no-compile [DEPRECATED] This flag doesn't do anything now. --force Forces major version upgrades --reset Hard resets git branch's to their new states overriding any changes and overriding rebase on pull --help Show this message and exit. In scenarios with many apps and sites in the same bench, I often use build --apps myapp --no-backup --reset --pull And then manually launch: bench build --apps myapp bench migrate --site mysite.com bench restart This way building and migrating process will be not launched for all apps and sites. Hi if anyone faces similar issue, Solution: If in between the fiscal year, you’re implementing and do a equalized division in monthly distribution, and test it by posting the expense more than the distributed % for a specific month it wont be trigerred as the months before that do have 100% budget left so is adjusted. To test it, simply divide Total Budget by Current + Remaining Months of the year then allocate the resultant for current and remaining months and months before current for them keep distribution ZERO. Now test the trigger of stop by making a posting exceeding the monthly accumularted allowance. image 1009×571 23.3 KB

By default, ERPNext applies line discounts at the item rate level, which means the rate of the item is reduced first and then extended to quantity. What I need instead is for the discount to apply to the item’s total amount , before taxes are calculated. In other words: Item Total = [(Rate x Quantity) - Discount] This should happen before taxes are applied. If the tax is inclusive, then additional calculations would be needed to adjust the item totals accordingly. Here’s a simplified example of what I need: Invoice Totals: Item Price : 250.00 Quantity : 9 Original subtotal : 9 × 250 = 2250 Discount applied to item total : –150 Net Item Total : 2100 Tax (18%) : 378 Grand Total : 2478 What I’m Looking For Is there a way in ERPNext to apply line discounts directly to item totals instead of item rates? Ideally, I want to support both flat amount (e.g. –150) and percentage discounts (e.g. –10%) . Should this be handled via a client script, server script, or is there a built-in feature I might be missing? Has anyone else implemented this? Any guidance would be appreciated. Thanks!

If the tax is inclusive, then additional calculations would be needed to adjust the item totals accordingly. Here’s a simplified example of what I need: Invoice Totals: Item Price : 250.00 Quantity : 9 Original subtotal : 9 × 250 = 2250 Discount applied to item total : –150 Net Item Total : 2100 Tax (18%) : 378 Grand Total : 2478 What I’m Looking For Is there a way in ERPNext to apply line discounts directly to item totals instead of item rates? Ideally, I want to support both flat amount (e.g. –150) and percentage discounts (e.g. –10%) . Should this be handled via a client script, server script, or is there a built-in feature I might be missing? Has anyone else implemented this? Any guidance would be appreciated. Thanks! Hi @gdelacruz-nts Both item line level and the whole document level discounts available in ERPNext and it can be applied either with a percentage of discount or discount amount either ways. Item level discount is located in item table where either discount amount or percentage can be inserted based on price list rate as following; image 1391×855 60.6 KB On the other hand, if discount is common for the whole Quotation then Additional Discount section is available under tax table where one can apply discount either on Net total (item table total before tax) or grand total (item table total + tax ). In your case, additional discount on net total where amount based discount is applied resulting a new net total as 2100 ; image 1277×879 51.3 KB ahsantareen: located in item table where either discount amount or percentage can be inserted based on price list rate as following; Hi @ahsantareen Thank you very much for your answer. However, this doesn’t solve my problem because using ERPNext’s current item line level discount, the price (or Price List Rate) of the item is changed. In this example, the rate would change by 100 (from 250 to 150), resulting in a final item total of 900.00. This is not the desired result image 1258×127 9.52 KB My task will only reduce the total at the item line level. Calculating that, 250 multiplied by 9 equals 2,250. After subtracting 150, the new total would be 2,100.00. We ran into this issue. In the end we had to do some custom work to keep the rate in another field and then calculate rate qty discount amount. Core will behave the way you have described. Hello @Muzzy Can you tell me how you achieve this behavior? What did you do? Is this problem resolved? I am experiencing the same issue @gdelacruz-nts . If it has been resolved, could you please describe how it was fixed here? Hi @gdelacruz-nts You have to play with Rate field to come to your desired Amount for the item line as following; image 1902×892 66.9 KB Otherwise custom script can handle such request. The issue is that when we add a discount or discount percentage, the item-wise total amount is updated, but the item rate also changes, which we do not want. In our case, the discount is derived from the Price List Rate, but when someone manually changes the item rate, the discount calculation still uses the original Price List Rate, and this causes the rate field to change unexpectedly on save. ​ For example: quantity 9 × rate 250 = 2,250. After applying a discount of 150, the new total should be 2,100, while the item rate should remain 250 and only the amount should be affected. ​ If there is any standard setting, script example, or recommended customization approach to apply item-wise discounts based on the line total (without modifying the item rate), suggestions would be appreciated.
